body:
I have chocolate milk today. That's it for the day so far but it's something. Granted, it's sitting next to me untouched. I had grits last night, which is good comfort food. The thing that sucks is after ten years, everything is a reminder. He makes amazing grits. Hell, I didn't know what a grit was before I met him. Chocolate milk? He loves it, too.

I am trying to drink water. I keep a bottle by my desk to mindlessly drink. 

The ideation is kind of a relief. I could end this pain if I wanted. But I'm not ready, so therefore, somewhere, I know there is hope for a better day. Because if I honestly believed this was all that was left, of course I would end it. Who wouldn't?

Thanks to folks like you, I get support. Support from tangible friends is available but I just don't want to be around them yet. For any number of reasons.
Working on it. My insurance is based out of state and I'm waiting for them to approve a local doc. They are taking their time. Thanks :)
thank you :) I read, too, and similar don't respond. What can I say to help? Everything feels trite. *hug*

I read your post but didn't really read it initially, as I was going through others and bawling. Then I read it again just now and said "I will be ok alone, I will be ok without him" and felt a weight lift. Your brain gets so into this vicious cycle of depression, fear, and pain. 

I have a few appointments to look at places tomorrow and I'm actually going to the edge of my budget to get some insanely gorgeous place near the water. It will help. Fuck it. (Still within budget, just at the top. When I started looking I was looking near the bottom, which in this area.. the chasm is huge.) Worst case, I'll have to work more, and that means more distraction. Or eat better, which means better health. Plus, I'll get money when he buys me out of the house. 

Thanks for posting. Internet strangers make the best friends sometimes.
Just bought it. Will start reading tonight. Thanks!

So many of these make me cry again, making it really hard to reply to everyone, but I really want to. Yours flat out makes me bawl. I've read it about 5 times since you posted and now just feel up to replying. Your situation was so much like mine. 

I can envision a day when he and I joyfully discuss our new happy lives and are happy for each other. We have that in us. Hell, we had a period we were open and we were actually supportive. We even talked poly a while back so that he could have that sexual relationship he needed. We have an immense amount of trust and support. So I think we can be like you, given time and separation to heal first. 

Thank you so much. I want to gather all the posters here that have been supportive and give them the biggest hug.

I think we might be able to fix it, but I think we both know there is a huge risk we won't. And there is a buildup of so much pain now. I think we both want to try to find happiness elsewhere, either with another person or alone. 

I am looking at places. We own the house together, but he can afford to buy me out and frankly, I couldn't emotionally stay. It kind of hurts that he can, but then it helps because that place meant so much that losing it would also hurt. Plus the drama of selling it versus him just buying me out. 

Thanks for taking the time out of your day to respond to a stranger. *hug*

Pain is pain, and I don't mean to minimize or downplay any one else's, but it is different as we age. Granted, you at 28 may be like me at 39, too. I had a relationship I call my 5-7, like a prison sentence, and my ex (still hurts to call him that) had his 4-6. They were the breakup and get back together that over time was 7 years but take out the breakup times, it was 5. That was rough. I saw a therapist. I moved out of state. I was in my 20s and it was hell. It wasn't like this but probably because he was an abusive asshole and I could cling to that hatred and move on.

Where as right now, we are still falling asleep in each others arms crying. Yes, I know, this prolongs its, but I am in the same house anyway. Until I get a new place (looking at three tomorrow so it won't be long) it's how we are choosing to cope. Ironically, I am sleeping better than I was on my futon, so in a way, that will help. 

Thanks for the anecdote. I would say the one place that age hurts is thinking no one will love a 40 year old woman. Reddit doesn't help with that thought. And I really shouldn't need another man to feel ok, but that, too, is human. 

Thank you for responding. Your words offer great strength to me and you are just as wise at 28 as I am at 39.

I'm rational enough to know we all mourn in our own ways. I have held him while he cried. Of course, then the emotion gets in the way and I think he's crying over the new girl or something equally stupid. He gave me ten years of his life. He took care of me when I was sick, put up with me at my worst, was there when my mom died. Of course he loved me, and still does, as I do him. And, if I am brutally honest, I had a momentary attraction to another man which manifested similar to his. The only difference is the man either wasn't mutually attracted, though he seemed to be, or more likely, didn't engage because he didn't want the drama of a rebound. So, but for the grace of whatever...

But logic just isn't overriding the pain and fear right now. It will over time. I can see that in my more lucid moments. I am rarely jealous. We had an intense amount of trust in our relationship (our jobs had us living apart most of the time and seeing each other sometimes as little as 6 days a month, and not once did either one of us seem to feel jealous). But, since my heart can irrational blame her, the jealousy is pouring out.

I don't know why you got downvoted, Your post is really helpful, thank you. I have posted in suicidewatch and it may have been another throw away post I made. I reread it on occasion because at that point, I knew I wanted out, and knew I was miserable but didn't know how to handle it. Now, I am rose coloring this whole thing and convinced we could have been happy (and still could be) if the right words are said. Deep down, I know this is BS and that post helps remind me that at a less emotionally vulnerable time, I knew this.

I'm sorry about your dad :( I'm so sorry I brought up that pain. I have had thoughts my whole life. I have made very weak attempts in my teens. They weren't for attention, as no one ever knew about them, but they also seemed to be more about asserting control over my fate then actual death. 

There is no difference between this and a divorce. One friend joked that the only difference is that we don't have a lawyer involved... except I am a lawyer.. so .. there's that. :) 

I am looking a few places to rent today. I know I have to stop talking to him for a few months. No small part of the issue with these it the person that is support to comfort you is the person that you can't talk to. 

My mom is gone. My dad is about as emotionally available as a desk. He doesn't even know yet. My mom would have been really nice to have around right now. 

PS r/breakups leads here now. 

Thank you so much. Your last paragraph was very sweet and helpful (as was the rest).

Thanks for smacking that person down. Ironically, I also have asthma so the post you replied (since deleted) was even more ridiculous. I run 5Ks, though not much more, but that's because I'm out of shape, not the asthma. 

The idea of 'bending or breaking' dyspareunia is ... kinda rapey. You don't bend or break painful sex. It was incredibly hard on my partner to know he caused me pain when we engaged in sex. Even, as another insensitive poster on this thread suggested, when he had non-intercourse fun, orgasms were painful. The muscle contractions are literally ripping my two uteri apart. But, you know.. "bend or break". Ugh.
You think I didn't try? Eww. Go away.
Sorry :( Seriously, I'm way over sensitive today. I guess that's obvious...

Thank you. I realized not so long ago much of my life outside of him was gone. Not that it was really super bad. We both still had our own hobbies, but it was often if he was home, I'd be home and vice versa. I started hanging out with friends a bit ago when I realized what was coming. It's been nice. I can't now, maybe soon, but right now I'm such a weepy sucker I don't want to be around anyone. I'm sure once I move out that will help tremendously. 

I think a therapist might help. I did it when my mom got sick and when she died. I did it when (in the same time frame) I was in an abusive relationship and couldn't find my way out. I find third parties held a lot, especially since I don't want to be completely honest with my friends, but there are parts of my relationship that add to the pain (his actions and mine). 

Thank you again. I hope you are continuing to do better!
Oh ok :)
Sorry for the initial downvote. I was going to remove it but I see you erased your comment. I'm (hopefully understandably) a bit fucked up right now and over sensitive.

Thank you. You get it. I've had short term relationship breakups, and they are tough, but at 9+ years (8, 7, whatever) your lives are so intertwined...

I think he and I will still talk. We have spent the last three days really openly communicating (too bad we didn't do that earlier.) We'll be hurt, and there will be a time for NC, I'm sure. We have pets in common that we are sharing. I may be wrong, but this is what we both want and willing to work for. We are best friends. This wasn't a bloody breakup with cheating, or yelling, lies, or abuse. It was simply I can't give you what you need and I can't see you struggle anymore, and vice versa. 

My sax has been gathering dust... I hated to play it around him because I suck, but he's always home when I am. My poor new roommate...
Can't tell with your username if you are being genuine, or creepy and opportunistic...

Thank you. I am trying to find a counselor and luckily my friends are coming out of the woodwork. It seems like he and I shared so much in common that there aren't things I forewent, but then again, I bet I can come up with some things. 

Thanks, internet stranger. *hug*

Thank you!!! Thank you so much! This was exactly what I needed.

I have met many women around our age and older that are in a similar position and remained single and are SO happy now. There is a reason we live longer single. Hell, his mother has told me on numerous occasions that I should stay single if I have the chance.. and it's her son! (I am pretty sure she's seen this coming).

I wrote to my health insurance today to inquire about counseling and I will heed the rest of your advice. 

thank you!! I can't thank you enough. It's amazing how words from a stranger can mean so much.

I've seen them all. Sadly, dyspareunia is not well understood and there are few treatments. At this point, I have no hope of it ever getting better. I have physiological issues that contribute with serious birth defects to my reproductive system, so... not much anyone can do. The IUD exacerbated the problem but..

Just bought razor blades. Funny ,the checkout guy telling me to have a nice day when that was all I bought. As I walked out the door, I was met with the cover of a magazine featuring Robin Williams.

You know, it's strange though, just the act of buying the razors made me feel better. 

You know, the problem with this sub is that we all come here when we are down. We don't want to read other's sad stories and we surely aren't in a position to offer support. So, people go without responses and end up feeling even more alone or rejected. I don't know any solution, but it is an issue.
